headline: Transformers and ensembles infer cell states across histology, spatial, RNA and chromatin data
label: Cross Modal Single Cell Inference
summary: Eight November 2026 reports use transformers, flow matching and ensembles to infer cellular profiles and labels across modalities and resolutions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring one layer of cellular information from another or from shared representations. GeneFlow predicts panels of up to 1,000 spatial genes from histology via flow matching, and st2sc resolves single-cell expression from multicellular spots. Bloom learns shared representations from paired expression and chromatin accessibility in about 300k mouse brain cells, SEMPER aligns protein language model embeddings with cell-type-specific interaction networks across 442 human brain cell types, and MCT models sets of cells to learn context-aware gene embeddings. A second, more heterogeneous strand improves label inference within scRNA-seq: scBoost stacks methods in an AdaBoost-inspired ensemble, scAdaG2M distills graph models into an MLP, and a fine-tuned Geneformer-V1 feeds class probabilities into clustering. What is new relative to earlier cancer-focused clone assignment is the shift toward transformer-based, cross-resolution inference in brain and spatial settings.
